mine_p14_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_001.text: Day 590 began with Lin paying Han the next four copper room and meal charge from the mine wages she had actually saved. The last four weeks of assistant work through Day 589 had paid thirty two, with sixteen in corresponding board, adding sixteen to the earlier forty saved after curriculum. Fifty six had stood in that reserve before the new room payment. The numbers did not promise a healthy day. They meant her ordinary bed would remain available if a difficult lesson ended badly, without borrowing against an unearned company comparison wage.

mine_p14_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_002.text: Lei had completed his seated sorting turns on Days 570, 577, and 584, earning the two coppers each for work actually done. The limited duty reassessments on Days 574 and 588 had been performed under their defined four copper fees. His four week transition still included the final Day 591 turn and actual board through Day 597. Two fingers remained gone. Lin watched him choose where to place the cup that morning and felt proud of his ordinary adaptation, then ashamed that part of her mind still wanted her own new route to answer it.

mine_p14_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_003.text: He asked whether the day's lesson would be a qualification attempt. Lin said no. It was a supervised bridge interruption preparation within the existing low input ceiling. Her current quantity had not met the preregistered local sixty usable and ninety one percent requirements, and she had not completed the three recovered changed condition trials or next day checks. Wei would assess actual preparation, not hand over a certificate for courage. Lei said that sounded safer than whatever answer he had expected. Lin smiled and kept the distinction clear even while longing for something more impressive herself.

mine_p14_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_004.text: The practice court was dry when she arrived. Guan had checked the grounded fixture and left the physical exit clear. A light cart sound passed beyond the outer gate; no mining load hung over the benches. Wei wore the slate blue tunic and had tied the loose grey strand back into her braid. She asked Lin to sit before opening the method book. The act slowed her arrival. Lin had walked quickly because she wanted the first bridge lesson after the loss review to feel like forward movement rather than another record of waiting.

mine_p14_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_005.text: Wei reviewed the course ledger. The eight copper instruction portion covered three maintenance appointments and twelve short supervised teaching visits, with their agreed task limits. The maintenance dates were complete. Nine teaching visits had been used: the five early preparation dates, then the sessions on Days 539, 546, 550, and 571. Today would be the tenth, leaving two for revised preparation if needed. The separate three qualifying site appointments and independent examination work remained finite and unused. The twenty four original fee had bought these specified services, not unlimited practice or the result Lin wanted.

mine_p14_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_006.text: Lin had forgotten how close the instruction list now was to its end. She asked whether two remaining visits would be enough. Wei said that depended on actual learning and could not be guaranteed in advance. If later work exceeded the course, another defined arrangement would have to be considered. For now the preparation task was within the bought curriculum. Guan set the two remaining visit spaces plainly on the ledger instead of hiding them behind an encouraging phrase. Lin felt the pressure, then named it aloud before it could become a reason to rush an unsafe continuation.

mine_p14_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_007.text: They reviewed stopping without qi. Wei asked Lin about her next accepted work possibility while she traced the taught references. Lin stopped the empty sequence, answered, and restarted as instructed. The cup remained untouched. A simple interruption could be survived when no input and no hope of a result made her hurry. Wei then asked what had changed in the weeks since the canopy failure. Lin spoke about the unbegun rescue impulse, the clinic journey, and the viable hand. She did not call grief a symptom the examiner could diagnose or a reserve that could power a new route.

mine_p14_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_008.text: Wei asked what the day's task was meant to establish. Lin answered that it would test stopping and resuming a taught bridge preparation under a bounded interruption, without claiming a completed small circuit. The examiner corrected one word: resumption would occur only after the full stop, release, rest, and current check allowed a new assigned start. It was not continuation held secretly beneath the conversation. Lin knew the rule and repeated it. The correction mattered because she had been imagining an elegant unbroken line, even in a task whose purpose included being able to end.

mine_p14_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_009.text: The body baseline came first. Lin reported normal sleep, a performed work week, no new pain, and no unusual sensory loss. Wei observed ordinary grip, touch comparison, leg movement, and the unhurried walk used in the method. She was assessing candidate control evidence, not issuing a medical diagnosis. The findings supplied a baseline for this supervised session. Lin had brought neither illness to conceal nor a guarantee that a new preparatory task would succeed. Guan checked the external field reference separately. Its clean response did not make Lin's internal bridge visible on the bench.

mine_p14_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_010.text: After the sampling discharge, fifty four and a half units were actually usable under the established six pair method, with ninety and a half percent compatibility. Both lay above the local six pair prerequisite and below the small circuit criteria. Wei wrote the actual values without multiplying compatibility into the usable quantity again. This would be a preparatory lesson under supervision, not one of the three qualifying trials. Lin read the line back. It kept the known method, the unfinished bridge, and the desired new qualification in three distinct places even though all belonged to her body.

mine_p14_011.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_011.text: The prepared task admitted at most half a unit across four ordinary breaths, with no more than an eighth in one breath. Its shoulder and waist fixture remained below shoulder height and grounded. No overhead catch or unassessed exertion was part of the lesson. At the assigned ordinary question Lin would stop input, release fully, and wait for the actual check before another instructed start. Wei said the cue in advance. Lin agreed while looking at the empty exit. The promise felt entirely within her control until the prepared portion was brought within reach.

mine_p14_012.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_012.text: The first breath admitted an eighth along the taught preparatory entry. Lin identified the familiar primary reference and the newly learned landmark, reporting only the assigned sensation. The fixture moved within its small bounded task. Wei watched the actual shoulder and waist posture while Guan counted the input against the prepared portion. The moment was not evidence of full circuit closure. Lin knew that, yet the orderly beginning made the blank continuation feel smaller. She wanted the next breath to prove she had finally learned to remain useful when the world interrupted her.

mine_p14_013.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_013.text: The second breath admitted another eighth. Guan asked the planned question about the next shift, and Wei gave the stop cue. Lin stopped the incoming portion but tried to keep attention poised at the incomplete bridge instead of ending the assigned sequence. She answered too quickly, then reached toward the imagined continuation before the required release and rest. It was a control error inside a taught preparation, not a brave necessary rescue. Wei stopped her again. No third or fourth input began. The failed resumption had already made Lin's wrist feel abruptly wrong.

mine_p14_014.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_014.text: Lin completed the grounded release on instruction through the established safe ending. The fixture had registered a sixteenth of useful work; the remaining three sixteenths of the quarter unit admitted left through release. The full quarter input was gone, counted once, not spent and then deducted again as if its discharge were another reserve. Fifty four and a quarter remained in the nominal accounting after that cost. It was not a current demonstrated usable quantity through a reliable route. Lin's new pain and failed control meant the method could no longer assume its former throughput available.

mine_exam_failure.speaker: narrator
mine_exam_failure.text: The preparatory bridge interruption failed on Day 590. Lin had not followed the full stop, release, rest, and check before trying to resume. The actual two eighth unit inputs stayed within the old ceiling, but controlled continuation did not. New wrist pain and altered touch accompanied the error; usable throughput through even the former assigned tasks was presently unvalidated and unavailable for application pending qualified assessment. Wei ended all input work. The six pair label remained the last qualification earned, not a claim that the injured learner could perform its tasks now. No small circuit certificate was issued.

mine_p14_016.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_016.text: Guan put the unused remainder of the prepared portion aside under its actual custody. He did not pour it into Lin because finishing the purchased half unit would make the account look tidy. Wei asked Lin to describe the wrist sensation while remaining seated and breathing ordinarily. She could feel touch, but one comparison differed from the baseline and moving her hand brought pain. Wei recorded the report and observation, stopped further body tasks, and requested qualified clinical assessment. The grounded court had kept the failed application bounded. It had not made the body incapable of being hurt.

mine_p14_017.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_017.text: Lin asked whether she should perform one familiar primary task to prove the old method still worked. Wei refused. A demonstrated new change after failed control was a reason to assess, not a challenge to defend a title. Lin had enough nominal reserve to tempt that argument. Nominal quantity did not restore a trustworthy current usable route. She put her uninjured hand against the bench and looked at the external comb. Its ordinary field response remained clean. The device could not settle the internal question or absolve her because it had not measured the harmed passage.

mine_p14_018.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_018.text: Mu entered the public waiting space for a screen invoice and saw the stopped setup. Guan gave her only the fact that Lin needed a clinic appointment. Lin chose to tell her the failed stopping sequence and new wrist change. Mu set the invoice aside and asked whether she wanted company on the ordinary walk. Lin did. The clinic stood a short surface walk away, not a distant journey requiring another miracle of timing. Guan sent the appointment message through the named contact while Wei retained the used input and failed control record under its appropriate custody.

mine_p14_019.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_019.text: Before leaving Lin apologized for wasting the tenth teaching visit. Wei said it had performed the actual work of revealing a failed preparation under supervision. The result was not bought success, and the interval would remain used. The two unused teaching visits could be rescheduled under the original terms after qualified recovery, not spent immediately trying to make today look better. Lin heard both kindness and a finite limit. She wanted the money returned to a morning when she had been healthy. The course could preserve unused services; it could not reverse a body error by refunding a clock.

mine_p14_020.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_020.text: The walk to Chen Ai's clinic felt longer than the path she had used with Deng. Mu matched Lin's pace and did not ask to test her hand on the way. A carter wanted them to step aside at the receiving corner. They moved onto the sound waiting patch rather than hurrying across the ruts. Lin's wrist hurt when she lifted her sleeve to show the clinic attendant where she felt the change. She wondered whether everyone could see how foolish the error had been. Most people saw two workers waiting through an ordinary cart passage.

mine_p14_021.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_021.text: Chen Ai received Lin after the appointment contact confirmed the stopped task and current symptoms. Wei's report described input, control failure, release, and ordinary baseline observations. It did not claim a clinical diagnosis. Chen assessed the tissue and sensory change within her own qualification, asking Lin to describe what happened without turning the lesson into a confession of character. Lin wanted to say she had been greedy. The clinician needed the movement, pain, touch, timing, and relevant method facts first. Moral language could wait until the body had an actual care plan.

mine_p14_022.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_022.text: The eight copper Day 590 appointment was paid from Lin's own saved common wage reserve. It was her private curriculum attempt, not an assigned gallery injury paid from Lei's company incident account. The distinction made her feel more alone until she understood the service was still actually available and paid. Chen would not ask whether she deserved care. Lin had fifty six before this period's four copper board and now the eight copper assessment, leaving forty four in that reserve. The unearned future comparison post supplied no money. Her earlier wages had done the useful thing she needed now.

mine_p14_023.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_023.text: Chen found a new ordinary tissue tenderness and a changed fine touch comparison requiring rest, protected movement, and next day reassessment. She did not diagnose meridian anatomy by looking at an external comb. Wei's route control record would remain separate and inform when supervised method checking could resume. Lin was told to stop input applications pending the actual assessments, avoid the affected movements, and report specified changes through the clinic contact. The immediate plan was outpatient care, not a dramatic admission followed by a convenient repeated discharge. She would sleep at the paid lodging with appropriate ordinary help.

mine_p14_024.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_024.text: The clinician arranged the next eight copper appointment for Day 591 and explained the actual ordinary warning signs that would require earlier contact. Lin kept the instruction sheet where she could find it without testing the hand against memory. The plan did not promise a stage advance after a night's rest. It gave the next examination of the actual body a date. Mu asked only the practical help Lin wanted shared at Han's room. Lin permitted the movement limit and appointment timing, withholding the rest of her private sensory history from the meal table.

mine_p14_025.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_025.text: At the courtyard contact Wei accepted the clinical practical limit and left the route work stopped. She would not independently treat the tissue or tell Chen which medical finding to reach. The failed preparation and its measured costs stayed in Lin's candidate record. The six pair qualification was not erased from history, but current usable throughput could not be used as if that history were a present operating condition. Lin could keep studying authorized references without input if attention and ordinary rest allowed. The independent examiner would wait for real recovery evidence before another actual route attempt.

mine_p14_026.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_026.text: Lin asked whether the new small circuit thresholds now had to be lowered. Wei said the day's failed control did not justify rewriting a preregistered criterion after seeing the result. The local sixty usable and ninety one percent standard stayed alongside the required three changed, recovered trials and next day checks. Preparation could be redesigned, delayed, or eventually abandoned. A certificate could not be made easier by calling pain the missing part of competence. Lin felt the loss of the shortcut before remembering she had never actually held it. The rule protected future workers as much as her own record.

mine_p14_027.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_027.text: Guan marked the used tenth teaching visit and the two remaining unused spaces. The three qualifying site slots still belonged to later qualifying dates, because today had been a bounded preparatory lesson below those criteria. The fixed independent examination portion retained its specified work: recovered candidate assessment, an instrument and control review, the three qualifying trials, and the final decision. He read those finite services back when Lin asked what the course still bought. Money remained attached to actual work, even when a learner no longer liked the history through which the work had become necessary.

mine_p14_028.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_028.text: Mu carried the instruction sheet while Lin kept her room key. The little division of work irritated her because she wanted her hands to do everything they had done that morning. Mu asked whether irritation changed the clinical limit. Lin laughed unwillingly and said no. They walked back without another practice attempt. At the receiving shelter Qiao was handling the outside roster. Lin chose to share the practical current movement restriction and ask about later ordinary work, keeping the private control account outside the employer's file. The failed lesson would not become a public spectacle merely because people knew her.

mine_p14_029.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_029.text: Qiao said the accepted four week block had ended on Day 589, with actual wages paid. No unscheduled shift would be marked as performed during this stopped period. When qualified advice allowed suitable work, they could agree a reduced task and hours. She gave the roster clerk only the practical absence information Lin authorized. The gap felt frightening, but she had a paid bed and personal reserve. Qiao would not hide work inside it or take over her private course. Lin could ask about employment without surrendering the body record.

mine_p14_030.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_030.text: At the receiving shelter an assistant had taken the sound count Lin would once have expected to handle. He asked whether she could help decipher a rubbed plate number before leaving. Lin could explain the source contact without lifting the object or taking over his task. She told him not to infer the digit from the next row. He sent it back for a label and thanked her. A practical piece of knowledge remained useful while her current input route was stopped. Lin felt the relief too strongly and had to resist making it proof that she should keep working.

mine_p14_031.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_031.text: Qiao saw the exchange and asked the assistant to continue under his own assigned hours. Lin's practical information could be offered once; it should not become an unrecorded shift performed by a recovering person who feared losing her place. Lin had not meant to create that arrangement. She recognized how easily usefulness could turn into a bargain nobody had named. Qiao gave her the next safe contact time for discussing suitable work after qualified advice. The current gap stayed honest. Lin left the receiving shelter with a useful answer given and no imaginary wage entered for it.

mine_p14_032.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_032.text: At Han's room Lei was practicing a permitted ordinary grip with his viable hand. He stopped when Lin entered and asked where she wanted to sit. She almost answered anywhere so he would not see the need, then chose the stool with her wrist supported as instructed. He moved his cup out of the way with his uninjured hand. The arrangement was unremarkable and difficult to accept. Lin had wanted to become the useful person beside his loss. Now he was making a place for her actual body, without asking her to earn the help by being brave.

mine_p14_033.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_033.text: Ma Lian came back from a meeting and heard the absence note. She wanted to visit, then asked the room contact instead of entering with a whole crew. Lin invited her for a short conversation. Ma had seen the canopy failure close enough to know how urgent skill could feel afterward. She said the mine still needed structural work, clear schedules, and sound response materials. A learner's new circuit would not replace those duties. Lin had been trying to become part of that response through a method it could not yet supply. Ma's words put responsibility back among several people.

mine_p14_034.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_034.text: Lin asked whether refusing an impossible rescue had been enough on Day 559. Ma said the chair and clear path had helped the actual crew and patient. Enough for those tasks was not the same as enough to stop every injury. She would not give Lin a heroic title or dismiss the wish as foolish. Ma had wanted to reach the rail faster too. The roof's moving condition had made speed without safe access dangerous. They sat with the account instead of inventing a cleaner version in which stronger affection created another route through timber.

mine_p14_035.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_035.text: Ma left before her next assigned work interval, keeping the visit as short as agreed. Lin watched her go and realized she had wanted Ma's witness to absolve her of the failed lesson as well as the alarm. Ma could speak about the ordinary evacuation she had actually led. She had not observed the bridge error or examined the wrist. Her kindness did not supply that evidence. Lin wrote the two events on separate pages again. They were emotionally linked in her life and causally different in their methods, costs, roles, and current consequences.

mine_p14_036.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_036.text: At the room door Diao brought a question about the public loss reference, then saw the supported wrist and asked whether this was a poor time. Lin said yes. He took the question to Ren instead of insisting it would only take a moment. The source work continued through the people assigned to it. Lin had feared every declined request would make an important fact vanish. Watching Diao turn calmly toward the proper contact challenged that fear. She was part of the mine's knowledge, not the only place it could be kept, and her private stopped period could be respected.

mine_p14_037.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_037.text: She told him the preparation had failed. He asked whether she had tried to heal his hand. She said no, and then admitted his injury had made finishing feel more urgent. Lei looked down for a long time. He said he did not want his missing fingers used as an employer for her body. The awkward phrase caught exactly what she had been doing. Lin had known the course was not treatment and still let love argue for speed. She thanked him for saying it, with none of the graceful composure she would have preferred.

mine_p14_038.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_038.text: Lei asked whether the taught input ceiling had been exceeded. Lin said only two eighth unit breaths had begun before the stop; the failure lay in control and premature attempted resumption. She gave the measured quarter input and full release cost plainly, without turning small numbers into proof that the event could not matter. Her nominal remaining reserve did not currently supply a usable assessed route. Lei nodded and asked whether the clinic had been paid. She said yes, from wages already saved. He looked relieved by a practical fact he could understand better than the unfinished bridge.

mine_p14_039.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_039.text: Han brought the meal covered by Lin's weekly arrangement and a spoon placed for the movement she could use. He had no special injury surcharge and no infinite free room to offer. The four copper board payment made the service available as agreed. Lin ate with the other hand where suitable and accepted help with the bowl when needed. She did not practice grip over supper to prove recovery. Every small adaptation felt like a visible failure until she watched Lei ignore the audience he no longer believed he owed. The room could feed a hurt person without examining her.

mine_p14_040.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_040.text: Mu returned to her screen work after making the practical handover. Lin thanked her for the walk and told her she need not cancel another paid repair to sit through the whole evening. Mu had a finite household too. She agreed to check in after her actual job, leaving Han and Lei aware of the shared practical limit. Lin felt safer because the arrangement named who would be present, rather than claiming love made everyone continuously available. A person could need help and still respect the work that let a friend remain housed and fed.

mine_p14_041.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_041.text: The afternoon light reached the private method book on Lin's shelf. She opened to the Day 590 entry and wrote the cause without ornament: the planned question, incoming input stopped, attention held at an incomplete bridge, premature attempted resumption, stop, release, new body change. It was not a meridian revelation, a trial narrowly passed, or a heroic effort foiled by an unlucky cup. The actual ordinary interruption had exposed a control weakness she needed to understand. Writing the account hurt her pride and kept the next attempt from inheriting a false explanation.

mine_p14_042.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_042.text: She wrote the accounting separately. After sampling, fifty four and a half had been actually usable under the established prerequisite check. Two eighth unit breaths admitted a quarter. A sixteenth became the fixture's observed useful work; three sixteenths left in the grounded release. The quarter was consumed once. The nominal remainder was fifty four and a quarter, while present usable throughput remained unavailable pending real assessment of changed control and tissue. A quantity left in an account did not mean a reliable application left in the person. That difference belonged at the center of the failure record.

mine_p14_043.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_043.text: Lei read only the practical portion she offered. He said the numbers were clear enough for a lampkeeper, then asked whether the record also included the desire to hurry. Lin showed him that sentence. He looked sad and said she could leave it there without making every later success a repayment to him. His own future would involve suitable work, ordinary care, and decisions about a changed hand. It would not become the audience for her cultivation. Lin had wanted him to approve the ambition. He gave her a kinder and harder thing: permission to let it be hers.

mine_p14_044.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_044.text: Outside, a hammer knocked against the repaired public gate. Lin flinched and then recognized the task. The sound did not prove the gallery failed again or the seam spoke. Han looked out and confirmed the worker's location before returning to the pot. Lin noticed how quickly remembered danger supplied an explanation to a new noise. The route lesson had exposed a similar hurry: familiar control made an unlearned continuation seem available. Different subjects shared one habit of mind. The analogy did not explain tissue injury, but it helped her name the urge to finish a story before the source arrived.

mine_p14_045.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_045.text: The lodging's younger carter returned in the repaired short sleeved shirt and asked Han for supper. He saw Lin's hand support and said the shirt looked less ridiculous beside it. Then he realized the joke had made her injury into his comfort and stopped. Lin said he could keep the useful part of the thought: a damaged thing or body did not need to look untouched to deserve life. His shirt and her route were different losses. He offered to fetch the bowl she could not carry, and she accepted the help without turning it into an agreement about everything.

mine_p14_046.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_046.text: Han read the practical room note and asked Lin which ordinary chores she wanted help arranging. She disliked the question because it made the next few days concrete. Laundry needed lifting wet cloth, and the bucket task involved a grip now excluded. They agreed Han's paid room service covered its established work, while Mu would help with one laundry transfer in a free interval she actually offered. Other tasks could wait or be separately arranged. Lin did not silently assign friends an indefinite domestic post. Making the limited help specific left fewer imagined obligations for everyone to resent later.

mine_p14_047.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_047.text: Lei asked whether she wanted the lamp near her bed earlier than usual. Lin said the light made reading tempting, and she had been told rest mattered more than studying every unused hour. He offered to place it where it lit the room path without shining directly on the method book. The ordinary adjustment surprised her into a smile. He knew what it meant to be tempted by a task she was not ready to resume. The lamp's light could serve getting a cup or finding the contact sheet, rather than recruiting the evening for another proof of commitment.

mine_p14_048.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_048.text: Mu returned with the finished screen invoice and told Lin the repair customer had complained about the visible patch. Mu had charged for a sound repair, not an invisible new panel. She offered the customer the agreed work record and refused to pretend old cloth was uncut. Lin listened without making the example identical to her body. The argument still felt relevant to how much effort she spent hiding a stopped route. A qualified record could contain an actual failure and remain worth reading. The invisible perfection she wanted would preserve appearance by removing the very evidence needed for revision.

mine_p14_049.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_049.text: Before Mu left, Lin asked whether she thought the bridge could recover. Mu said she hoped so and had no qualified answer. The simple distinction was harder than a reassuring promise. Lin thanked her for keeping hope available without dressing it as a finding. Tomorrow Chen would examine actual change, and later Wei would assess the method when qualified care allowed it. Lin could bring her fear to friends and her body to the people qualified to evaluate it. Neither group had to impersonate the other in order to matter. The room felt quieter once that expectation was put down.

mine_p14_050.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_050.text: Chen Rui sent a permitted factual question through the employer contact about the postponed comparison proposal. Qiao answered only that no qualified candidate post had been accepted and ordinary site work remained dependent on its separate assessment. Lin's private injury findings did not travel to his client through that question. If she later wished to discuss her own availability, she could do so under actual terms. The future proposal had not become a creditor entitled to her body report. Lin was glad of the boundary and disappointed that the attractive work now felt farther away. Both feelings were possible.

mine_p14_051.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_051.text: Sui saw the public practical restriction and asked Lei whether Lin's six pair label had been false. Lei said the label was an earlier qualification, and current injury could make a previously taught task unavailable. Sui should ask the appropriate public work contact about assigned duties, not demand private clinical proof at supper. Lei had chosen to share only that practical distinction. Lin overheard from the doorway and thanked him later. He shrugged, saying people had been asking the same foolish kind of question about his viable hand. They were learning to keep history and present ability in different sentences.

mine_p14_052.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_052.text: Mu returned from the contact window with Lin's authorized lodging acknowledgement and appointment confirmation. The Day 591 reassessment time was confirmed, and the ordinary instructions remained in force. No second appointment had been performed yet, and its reserved eight coppers were not treated as a current diagnosis. Lin counted the forty four remaining in her common reserve and set aside the next fee. The amount made the coming morning less uncertain without making its findings predetermined. She would need ordinary care paid for what it actually did, and patience paid for with time nobody could return unused.

mine_p14_053.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_053.text: Guan sent the authorized failure reference for Lin to compare with her account. The quantities and cue agreed; she corrected a phrase implying a third input had begun. It had not. The correction did not minimize pain or turn failed control into success. Accurate bounds mattered for medical interpretation, later preparation, and the examiner's decision. Guan retained the corrected course copy; Lin kept the authorized candidate version. The mistake would keep its particular shape, rather than growing with each frightened retelling until no actual lesson could be learned.

mine_p14_054.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_054.text: Later Mu found Lin staring at the closed method book and asked whether she wanted conversation or quiet. Lin chose conversation about work, relieved to leave her body alone for a while. Mu described another frame measured correctly and cut badly, leaving the cloth unable to fit without another repair. It concerned a different material and a different loss. Lin listened as a friend, letting the story retain its own meaning rather than converting every imperfect object into a lesson about meridians. The room had space for more than her failed bridge.

mine_p14_055.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_055.text: When Mu asked later what frightened her most, Lin said the usable route might never return. Chen had not predicted that, and Wei had not certified it. It was a fear, not an actual finding. Mu asked whether Lin wanted it written as such. She did. Naming the uncertainty did not soothe it immediately. It stopped the fear from becoming an authoritative sentence repeated to everyone who offered help. Tomorrow's qualified assessment would examine the actual changed body. Recovery would need funded care, suitable duties, and repeated evidence, not a promise chosen tonight because silence was intolerable.

mine_p14_056.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_056.text: Han checked that Lin could reach the ordinary instruction sheet, water, and room contact without the excluded movement. He did not test her wrist himself. Lei showed her where his stable cloth support had proved useful, then remembered their injuries were different and asked the clinician's practical advice before suggesting any use. Lin appreciated him stopping his own analogy. The fact that ordinary care had helped his viable hand did not prescribe her route recovery. Similar need could produce company and useful questions while the actual qualified plan remained specific to the person who had been hurt.

mine_p14_057.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_057.text: Lin put the unopened compatible portion out of reach with its owner and course custody intact. Nothing would be consumed at the lodging to see whether the pain had improved. The remaining finite consumables belonged to the unused preparation and qualifying work, subject to later matched condition checks. She could read an authorized sheet and rest without borrowing fuel from a future trial. The simple decision made her feel temporarily less like a practitioner, then more accountable. Her method now included an actual stopped period. A label that could not survive that truth would not be worth earning.

mine_p14_058.speaker: narrator
mine_p14_058.text: Wei's final message that evening concerned practical reporting, not consolation through a future result. She confirmed the full stop on input, the separate clinical plan, and the need for ordinary next day findings before any later method check. Lin was still recorded at the last earned six pair stage. Current usable throughput remained unavailable. The local small circuit criteria stayed preregistered, and no passed trial had occurred. The examiner had left Lin with present facts and a future she would have to build through actual recovery. That was harder to bear than a promise, and much more useful to keep.

mine_p14_059.speaker: narrator
